details.summary: The idea that creative people are right-brained and logical people are left-brained is neuroscience fiction. Brain imaging shows that creative tasks activate both hemispheres extensively. Creativity requires the integrated cooperation of the entire brain, not one side.
details.whyItMatters: The right-brain myth limits people by making them believe they are either creative or analytical. Debunking it frees everyone to develop both capacities without neurological excuses.
takeaways: Brain imaging shows creativity uses both hemispheres
No individual is dominated by one brain hemisphere
The myth originated from misinterpreted split-brain research

faq.question: Where did the right-brain myth come from?
faq.answer: Roger Sperry's split-brain research in the 1960s showed hemispheric specialization in patients whose brain connections were severed. Pop psychology exaggerated these findings into a false binary of creative right-brains versus logical left-brains.

faq.question: Do the brain hemispheres differ at all?
faq.answer: Yes. Each hemisphere has some specializations, such as language processing in the left hemisphere for most people. But these are tendencies, not absolutes, and complex tasks like creativity always involve extensive communication between both sides.
